findings.title: Permission check uses AND instead of OR, breaking team admin/owner authorization
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. A user can be an admin OR an owner, but these two role checks are typically mutually exclusive (owner is a separate role from admin), so logically ANDing them means this will almost always evaluate false, denying legitimate team admins/owners the ability to add guests unless they happen to satisfy both roles. This should be `||`.

findings.title: Guest emails leak into console log on error, and errors swallowed silently
findings.body: On failure to send add-guest emails, the catch block just does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without logging the actual error or using the project's logger (`@calcom/lib/logger` used elsewhere). This hides failures from monitoring and makes debugging email delivery issues difficult; it should use the structured logger and include the error object.

findings.title: No input sanitization/limit on number of guests added
findings.body: The schema (addGuests.schema.ts) only validates each guest is a valid email but places no limit on the number of guests that can be added in one call. A malicious or buggy client could pass thousands of emails, causing a large bulk createMany and spamming hundreds of emails per booking with no rate limiting, unlike other similar endpoints that usually cap list sizes.

findings.title: Guests added to calendar/video event but no error handling around eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees
findings.body: The call to `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is unguarded; if the underlying calendar/video provider call throws, the whole mutation fails even though the DB has already been updated with the new attendees (see the `prisma.booking.update` call above). This creates a data inconsistency where guests exist in the DB as attendees but the calendar event/invite was never updated, with no rollback or compensation logic, and no user-facing distinction between a DB failure and a calendar sync failure.

findings.title: Error toast interpolates raw backend message key without translation fallback safety
findings.body: `t(err.message)}` passes `err.message` directly to the translation function; if the backend throws a message that isn't a translation key (e.g. a raw error string, Prisma error, or unexpected exception message), `t()` will just return the untranslated string, which is fine, but combined with `err.data?.code` prefix this could show raw/confusing text (e.g. 'undefined: NOT_FOUND') to users for errors not explicitly mapped to i18n keys, as there's no safe default handling for the generic case.

findings.title: Guest email case-sensitivity not normalized when deduping / blacklist check
findings.body: `uniqueGuests` compares `guest === attendee.email` directly without lowercasing, while blacklist check lowercases only the blacklist entries but not the incoming guest emails (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). This means mixed-case guest emails can bypass both the duplicate-attendee check and the blacklist filter, allowing duplicate or blacklisted guests to be added via case variation.
